title: edge-streaming-resequence-and-reconnect-amplification-digest
summary: A P0 degradation impacted hosted streaming sessions in us-west1 on 2026-10-14. Symptom: clients received duplicate or out-of-order stream fragments and premature terminal events leading to reconnect storms and gateway 5xx amplification. This document records timeline, evidence, root cause, immediate mitigations and next-runbook changes.
impact: Incident window ~52 minutes (2026-10-14T02:17Z to 2026-10-14T03:09Z). Approximately 0.9% of streaming sessions experienced duplicated fragments or out-of-order seq numbers. p95 token latency for impacted sessions increased by ~540ms. Gateway 502/504s spiked due to acceptor queue overload from reconnect storms. No persistent data corruption; duplication handled at persistence layer.
timeline: 02:14Z - Minor p50 latency blips observed on streaming edge (alerted but not paged)
02:17Z - SRE oncall paged: surge in reconnects and 5xx for v1/stream/chat
02:19Z - Identified primary region us-west1 and edge-cluster-32 as hotspot; enabled traffic-fence to healthy cluster
02:22Z - Traces show resequence patterns (seq N, N+1, N repeated) and duplicate fragments
02:28Z - Noticed edge multiplexer deploy (PR #412) had rolled to cluster at ~02:09Z; correlation established
02:34Z - Rolled back PR #412 in affected cluster and toggled conservative ordering flag; reconnect rate decreased
02:45Z - Proactively applied mitigations to adjacent clusters and monitored stabilization
03:09Z - Metrics returned to baseline; pager cleared and follow-ups opened
root_cause: An optimization in the edge multiplexer changed failover/shutdown ordering and allowed an in-flight buffered fragment to be flushed and re-transmitted after a failover. The behavior violated per-session monotonic delivery assumptions. Older SDKs treated resequence as fatal and closed sessions, producing reconnect storms. The reconnect storms increased acceptor queue pressure, causing transient 502/504s at the gateway.
evidence: Traces: example trace ids 8a3f2c and 8a3f31 show seq pattern 12,13,12 within same session
Deployment logs: PR #412 rollout timeline matches incident start (edge-cluster-32 deployed ~02:09Z)
SDK telemetry: clients on SDK versions <2.7.0 more likely to close sessions on resequence
Acceptor metrics: ephemeral backlog increased ~7x during reconnect peak correlating with gateway 502 spike
Persistence checks: no duplicate writes in storage; dedup at persistence layer worked as intended
Repro harness: internal failover replay reproduces resequence within ~60s when running multiplexer changes
mitigation: Immediate rollback of multiplexer PR #412 in affected clusters (performed 02:34Z)
Enable conservative per-session ordering flag on edge multiplexer instances
Traffic fencing: route new sessions away from impacted cluster during investigation
Short advisory to customers: recommend SDK >=2.7.0 which tolerates resequence with idempotency tokens
Throttle reconnect bursts at edge acceptor to protect upstream control plane and reduce amplification
runbook_draft: Add a new runbook section 'stream-resequence-detection' with thresholds: duplicate-chunk-rate > 0.2% for 5m triggers page
Triage checklist: determine if resequence source is multiplexer change, network reorder, or client bug
Play: run automated traffic-fence to evacuate sessions from suspect edge cluster and scale acceptors before rollback
Rollback procedure: safe rollback steps for multiplexer with post-rollback synthetic long-lived stream validation
Validation: trace queries to confirm monotonic seq and a synthetic-suite of 10+ long-lived streams as smoke
follow_up_actions: Implement sequence fencing in multiplexer to guarantee monotonic per-session delivery — owner: Ethan Zhao — due: 2026-11-01
SDK fix: release defensive de-dup/idempotency handling and default idempotency token usage — owner: Anika Patel — due: 2026-10-28
Observability: add streaming resequence alert and auto-sample traces when triggered — owner: Luis Romero — due: 2026-10-21
Acceptor rate-limiter: implement backoff/queue-hysteresis for reconnect storms — owner: Maya O'Connor — due: 2026-11-08
Cross-team postmortem session with multiplexer, SDK and edge teams scheduled 2026-10-18 16:00Z — facilitator: Priya Singh
oncall_notes: Keep metrics and tracing enabled during triage; traces were crucial to find ordering anomalies
When rolling back edge components run real long-lived stream smoke tests (10+ sustained) before declaring success
If acceptor backlog > 3x baseline, enable temporary throttles to prevent gateway 5xx amplification
Customer communication: provide concise recommended SDK version, short repro steps and expected mitigation timeline
